decisions.reason: Selecting a satin finish and gold distribution does not change the required geometric peak alignment between the Hero V and É accent.
The material distribution reinforces visual emphasis but does not change the second V's established geometric height and prominence relationships.
Applying champagne gold to the second V right arm does not change the second V's geometry, construction method, or relationship to the Hero V.
The selected gold application does not alter the requirement that the É accent reuse the exact Hero V terminal geometry.
The source explicitly selects a material finish and distribution while retaining the exact geometry; it does not modify the Hero V construction.
Keeping non-gold elements black is part of the material-treatment Requirement and does not change the E and L letterform architecture.
The material selection itself does not alter kerning; the same message's separate kerning failure and refinement decision are already represented in this candidate's history.
Distributing gold across the three signature elements changes their material appearance, not the shared terminal's geometric shape or refinement constraints.
The chosen finish and gold distribution do not change the established E and L cap-height alignment rule.
The material-treatment decision does not alter the common baseline alignment of the wordmark.
The source's design selection and requests do not change the obligation to include rationale with review rounds.
